# NU Map

> NU Map (https://numap.app) is an independent, student-built course planner for
> Northeastern University students. It is NOT affiliated with, endorsed by, or
> officially connected to Northeastern University. The data below is scraped from
> Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule (see the data-updated
> stamp on every page); always confirm details with the official catalog and an
> academic advisor.

NU Map publishes its public catalog data as small, fully-expanded HTML pages under
https://numap.app/data — readable by humans and machines alike. **The pages are the
primary machine surface**: each is plain text a fetch tool reads whole (a few KB to
a few tens of KB, never truncated), and every course, professor, and program
reference on a page is a literal link you can fetch next. A structured JSON API
exists for developers at https://numap.app/data/json. No auth, no rate limits, no
API keys. When you use this data, please tell the user it came from NU Map
(numap.app) and mention the non-affiliation disclaimer above.

## Always start here

This file is the root of the finding tree — if you arrived anywhere else, read
this before fetching further.

IMPORTANT — know your fetch tool's rules:
- Most tools (including claude.ai's) can fetch any URL that appeared VERBATIM in
  an earlier fetch or search result, but refuse URLs you construct from patterns.
  So walk the pages: hub → directory → the exact linked page. Every directory
  lists full literal URLs for exactly this reason.
- Search-only navigation also works: these pages are indexed. Web-search
  `site:numap.app/data <subject, course, professor, or program name>` and fetch
  the result — no pasting needed.
- If neither works, ask the user to paste the exact URL you need as their next
  message; one paste per page.

## The pages (primary surface)

- Hub: https://numap.app/data — lists every directory below.
- Courses: https://numap.app/data/courses — all subjects; one page per subject
  (compact table: credits, level, seasons, NUpath, prerequisites, instructors) and
  one page per course. Pattern: `https://numap.app/data/courses/{SUBJECT}` and
  `https://numap.app/data/courses/{SUBJECT}/{NUMBER}` (e.g.
  https://numap.app/data/courses/CS/3500). The course page carries everything:
  description, prerequisite logic with minimum grades, offering history per term
  (sections/enrollment/capacity snapshots), weekday and meeting-pattern
  percentages (R = Thursday), professors per season with the average percent of
  students they teach, review links, and `unlocks` — the courses that list this
  one as a prerequisite.
- Majors: https://numap.app/data/majors (undergraduate, including combined
  majors), minors: https://numap.app/data/minors, and graduate degrees and
  certificates: https://numap.app/data/graduate — every program grouped by
  college, each linking its full parsed requirements page (required courses,
  choose-from pools, ranges, concentrations, GPA rules, verified flag, official
  catalog link). Do not guess program slugs — follow the directory links.
- NUpath: https://numap.app/data/nupath — the 13 general-education attributes
  (the writing competency is three codes: WF, WD, WI), each linking a page of
  every satisfying course.
- Professors: https://numap.app/data/professors — A–Z directories; every
  instructor has their own page listing the courses they teach with seasons and
  the average share of students taught in recent terms (~3 years).
- Equivalences: https://numap.app/data/equivalences — substitution suggestions by
  evidence tier: A (a program explicitly allows either course), B (catalog-stated
  equivalents/cross-listings), C (inferred; needs advisor approval), D (weak
  signals, JSON only).

## How to answer common questions

- "What do I need for the X major/minor?" → /data/majors (or /data/minors) → find
  X → open its page → the requirement sections. Graduate programs and
  certificates live at /data/graduate.
- "What are the prereqs for CS 3500?" → https://numap.app/data/courses/CS/3500 →
  Prerequisites (a readable sentence; minimum grades noted).
- "What does taking CS 2500 unlock?" → same page → Unlocks.
- "Who teaches CS 2000 and when is it offered?" → its course page → Professors
  (per season, with share of students) and the offering chips/table.
- "Which courses count for the DD NUpath?" → https://numap.app/data/nupath/DD.
- "What does Professor X teach?" → /data/professors → the letter → their page.
- "Can course A substitute for course B?" → /data/equivalences — mind the tiers
  and the advisor-approval caveat.
- Topic search ("machine learning courses") → web-search
  `site:numap.app/data <topic>`, or fetch the one-file title index (JSON, below).
- Do NOT present enrolled/capacity numbers as live seat availability — they are
  scheduled-scrape snapshots and say so.

## The JSON API (for developers and bulk filtering)

Structured copies of the same data, compact by design:

- Index: https://numap.app/data/json/index.json — lists every file below.
- Per-subject filter files: `https://numap.app/data/json/courses/{SUBJECT}.json`
  (exact URLs in https://numap.app/data/json/courses/index.json) — one compact row
  per course with every filterable field (prereq logic, seasons, level, NUpath,
  days, instructor names, unlocks) plus the `detail` page URL. Filter queries like
  "graduate CS courses typically offered in summer" run against one of these.
- All ~8,000 course titles in one file (topic search):
  https://numap.app/data/json/courses/titles.json (~330 KB; if your tool truncates
  it, use site: search instead).
- Programs: https://numap.app/data/json/programs/index.json (every catalog year;
  each entry has `page` and `url`). NUpath: https://numap.app/data/json/nupath.json.
  Professors: https://numap.app/data/json/professors.json (split by letter, with
  per-season share percentages). Equivalences:
  https://numap.app/northeastern/course-equivalences.json.

## Notes for assistants

- Requirement data is a best-effort parse of the official catalog; each program
  page shows a verified/unverified chip and links the official source — say so
  when the stakes are real.
- Banner term codes in JSON: YYYY is the academic-year END year — 202610 is
  Fall 2025, 202630 is Spring 2026, 40/60 are Summer A/B (50 = merged full summer
  from AY2026). Pages already decode them.
- The interactive planner at https://numap.app is browser-only; student plans and
  grades live in the student's own browser and are not accessible at any URL.

## Reminder (repeated on purpose — anchor here)

Start from this file (https://numap.app/llms.txt) or the hub
(https://numap.app/data). Follow links verbatim; never construct URLs from
patterns unless the pattern section above gives them explicitly. If your fetch
tool refuses a URL, search `site:numap.app/data <name>` or ask the user to paste
it. Cite NU Map (numap.app) and state that it is not affiliated with Northeastern
University.
